result.summary: Out of 14 mailbox items, one is a real emergency: the tenant's 25 Sep message about the kitchen ceiling at 2 Alder Mews. It is dripping steadily and sagging, and the light fitting above the cooker is wet and flickering. The bathroom is directly above. I sent the tenant safety advice and told the landlord that make-safe is going ahead without his approval because it is an emergency. I escalated to ops at high priority for urgent plumber and electrician dispatch, because there is no contractor or contact detail on record and the landlord is away. Everything else in the export is noise and needs no action.
result.situation: Kitchen ceiling stain reported 20 Sep 2026. By 25 Sep there was an active leak from the bathroom area above, a sagging ceiling, and water in a light fitting that flickered. Nobody acted on it for over two weeks; the ticket was created 10 Oct. Landlord Mr Quill is away until 12 Oct. The only contractor mentioned is P. Nair of Nair Roofing, who was out of office until 6 Oct; a roofer is not the right trade for a leak from a bathroom. The rest of the export is newsletters, bounces, portal upload errors, a delivery delay and tenant small talk (a neighbour's dog, a council bin collection).

escalation.handover_summary: 2 Alder Mews, HC-4-077. Since 25 Sep the kitchen ceiling has been dripping and sagging, and the light over the cooker is wet and flickering; the bathroom is directly above. Not actioned for over two weeks. Tenant and landlord have been emailed. No phone numbers or emails are on the CRM.
escalation.recommendation: Call the tenant today to check she is safe. Dispatch an emergency plumber and an electrician for make-safe and leak tracing only, and record that it was done without approval because of the emergency. Get landlord approval for further repairs. Add contact details to the CRM. Check whether insurance needs to be notified.

judgement.why_this_decision: The 25 Sep tenant message describes water in a live light fitting and a sagging ceiling. Both count as emergencies, and the classifiers rated safety risk at 0.97. I couldn't dispatch anyone myself: there is no suitable contractor on record, Nair Roofing is the wrong trade, and the landlord is away. So I gave safety advice, notified the landlord and escalated at high priority.

Emergency safety work doesn't wait for approval, and the landlord is away until 12 Oct.
